records.quote: To summarize, BASS-II's approach, microgravity combustion tests were performed aboard the International Space Station.
Study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity.
records.derivation: Objective 1) of the record; names the phase. Caution: test F4 is a 'Japan Wax candle' (PSI table material column); no source sentence states the phase of the candle fuel (see not_found).

records.quote: Solid fuel ignition uses a Kanthal hot wire.
records.derivation: Pre-flight science requirements slide (dated 4/14/2010), 'General Requirements' bullet; corroborates R2.

records.quote: International Space Station (ISS)
Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)
records.derivation: The record approach adds: 'The wind tunnel was installed in the Microgravity Science Glovebox which supplied power, imaging, and a level of containment.'

records.quote: Main variables are airflow speed and oxygen concentration (oxygen varied below 21% by adding nitrogen).
records.derivation: Nitrogen is the gas added to the ambient to lower O2. Same in the record objective: 'Ambient oxygen concentration (via working volume nitrogen vitiation)', and SRD page=1: 'GN2 is used to vitiate the MSG working volume to desired O2levels.' (text layer as extracted). Tests left in unvitiated ambient air also have N2 as balance (air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen).

records.quote: Sandra Olson burned three sizes of pmma rods (mostly clear), igniting the upstream end for a stagnation flame / concurrent flow geometry.
records.derivation: test_id: ReadMe paragraph=15 'Test number:   Initial of PI name followed by test number from the initial matrix.'; PSI table PI column 'Olson' carries O1..O22 (with a/b repeats). Corroboration, SRD page=12 Olson matrix note: 'ignite at a consistent concurrent flow, then reduce to low flows and measure spread, repeat until extinguished.' Caution, same page: 'in the event of a non-ignition of the rod at low O2, an opposed ignition will be attempted, followed by an ambient air opposed or concurrent test at TBD flow(s).', so individual O tests may deviate.

records.quote: Carlos Fernandez-Pello burned three sizes of pmma rods (mostly black), igniting the downstream end for an opposed flow flame spread geometry.
records.derivation: test_id: PSI table PI column 'Fernandez-Pello' carries P1..P25 (prefix P, not F; F is Ferkul). Corroboration read from the SRD page=16 matrix image (no text layer): 'ignite at a consistent OPPOSED flow, then reduce to low flows and measure spread, repeat until extinguished.'

records.quote: priority order test matrix per PI: Miller [...] Priority Sample # width (cm) thickness (mm) backing flow velocity (cm/s) Direction oxygen % # sides to burn Notes 1 15 2 5 mica 10 (ramp down) opposed 21 one need mica out the back
records.derivation: Only the slide title is in the PDF text layer; the table is an image and the header plus first row were transcribed from it. The Direction column reads 'opposed' in all 20 rows. It is the pre-flight priority matrix, and no source maps its rows (Priority / Sample #) to the flown M test numbers. ReadMe paragraph=7 ('Fletcher Miller burned various thickness and widths of thick pmma slabs (one sided and two sided burns).') states no flow configuration. ReadMe publication titles (paragraphs 54, 59: '... Intermediate Thickness PMMA Sheets ... in Microgravity Opposed Flow') point the same way but are titles only. test_id: PSI table PI column 'Miller' carries M1..M20.

records.quote: Fuel samples were mounted inside a small wind tunnel which could impose airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s.
records.derivation: Capability of the wind tunnel ('could impose'), not a statement of the speeds actually tested; only the upper bound is written, no lower bound. Caution: the PSI table 'Air display' column (not extracted) has readings above 40 in some tests, e.g. T17 '6   53' and T21 '11   max(47)', so 40 cm/s should not be treated as a verified bound on tested flows. The wind tunnel is the BASS hardware launched for SPICE (see lineage).

Stated discrepancy, not averaged: the Fig. 2.20 caption (pdf page 49) gives the SDSU 1g tests in 20.7 percent O2 and 79 percent N2 at 1 atm, while the text on page 46 says 101 kPa and 21 percent O2.

records.quote: PMMA (NASA) in 0g on International Space Station, 2-cm sample with 10.x cm in 20.7 percent O2 and 79 percent N2 at 1 atm. (a) Burning and Suppression of Solids—II (BASS–II) B03 sample; 100 µm thick. (b) BASS–II B11; 200 µm thick. (c) BASS–II B4; 300 µm thick. (d) BASS–II B13; 400 µm thick.
records.derivation: Figure 2.20 caption text (section 2.3.7, printed page 41), not a value read from the image. NOMINAL condition: one set of conditions is written for all four panels. test_id: the caption writes 'B03'; the PSI table writes 'B3' (row 3, '100 micron film   2 cm wide', thickness matches the caption's 100 µm). B11, B4, B13 are written as in the table and their table thicknesses (0.2 mm, 300 micron, 0.4 mm) match the caption. Caution on how generic the caption is: it gives 20.7 percent O2 for all four, while the PSI table 'Calibrated initial O2 % by vol' is 22.2 for B3 and B4 and 21 for B11 and B13. DISCREPANCY with R302 (measured total pressure 99.2 to 99.5 kPa stated on page 46 for 'the tests reported' in the same section): both are proposed, none chosen.

records.quote: The total pressure is also monitored, which varied from 99.2 to 99.5 kPa in the tests reported.
records.derivation: MEASURED (monitored) total pressure, section 2.3.5 'Microgravity and Normal-Gravity Experiments', in the paragraph describing the BASS-II opposed-flow duct in the ISS (preceding sentences on the same page describe the O2 sensor and the hot wire anemometer; next sentence: 'Experiments were conducted in the Microgravity Science Glovebox of ISS by two crew members.'). Scope is ambiguous: 'the tests reported' is not listed. The only flight tests identified by number in section 2.3 are B03 (=B3 in the PSI table), B11, B4 and B13 (Figure 2.20 caption, page 49); Figure 2.19 (page 48) also shows a microgravity 100-µm test at 3 cm/s without a test number. Not applied to the 1-g downward tests, which the same page gives separately as 'pressure 101 kPa' (already record R204 in PSI-25.extractor.json). DISCREPANCY with R301 (nominal '1 atm' in the Fig. 2.20 caption for the same four tests). test_id is a lower bound: the reported set also includes unnumbered 100-um tests spanning ~40 to ~1 cm/s (verificador).

records.quote: The tests were conducted in ambient O2 molar fraction of 16 to 21 percent. Ambient pressure was 1 atm.
records.derivation: Section 7.1.3 'Experimental' (printed page 94) of the T'ien SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric chapter; same paragraph block opens with 'All tests were conducted in a small flow duct (shown in Figure 7.1) within the MSG aboard the ISS.' (page 102). Nominal value; no measured pressure is given for these tests. test_id: section 7.1.4 (page 103) says 'A total of 27 tests were carried out for the fabric samples in BASS–II [...] These are listed in Table 7.1.' Table 7.1 (page 104) writes ids as 'GMT<day>-T<n>' (e.g. 'GMT45-T1', 'GMT216-T28a'); the PSI table writes 'T1', 'T28a'. The GMT day of each row matches the PSI table GMT column (e.g. T1 45, T5 100, T9 175, T11 178, T19 190, T25 216) and the O2 column matches the table 'Calibrated initial O2' (e.g. T1 18.5, T4 18.7, T13 17.5, T24 18.2); 27 BASS-II rows, matching the stated total. EXCLUDED: the four rows labelled 'BASS' at the bottom of Table 7.1 (GMT96-T8, GMT96-T7, GMT131-T10, GMT222-T11) are BASS (PSI-26) tests that reuse T numbers; and PSI table tests T3 and T7 ('4 cm spherical section') are not in Table 7.1, so not covered. Side note, not pressure: Table 7.1 gives width 2.2 cm for T24 while the PSI table material says '1 cm SIBAL   top side ign'; the mapping relies on GMT day + T number.

records.quote: Flame appearance, flame growth, and spread rates were determined in both the opposed and concurrent flow.
records.derivation: Investigation-level sentence: it says opposed AND concurrent flow both occurred, not which test had which. Paired with R402 (same sentence, concurrent). Same idea in the Summary Report page=13: 'These samples could generally be mounted so that they could be burned in either the opposed or concurrent flow direction.' Per-test records follow (R403 onward).

records.quote: Flame appearance, flame growth, and spread rates were determined in both the opposed and concurrent flow.
records.derivation: Same sentence as R401; it covers both directions for the investigation as a whole, without saying which tests were concurrent.

Only ReadMe publication titles (paragraphs 37, 51, 52, 57) mention opposed-flow flame spread; they are titles, not statements about these tests. lineage: BASS-II reused the on-orbit BASS hardware originally launched for SPICE: 'BASS-II will utilize the on orbit BASS hardware launched originally for SPICE on STS-126.' (SRD page=9); 'The acquisition rate of 4 Hz can not be changed from SPICE/BASS.' and 'The measurement accuracy of ±10% was met by the SPICE hardware prior to its launch.' (SRD page=1); video field of view and D300s still-image requirements are the same as BASS (SRD page=1). not_found.looked_in: Summary Report full text searched for 'kPa', 'atm', 'pressure', 'psi', 'torr' (all hits reviewed). Only B3 (written 'B03') and B4 are named next to a pressure, in the Figure 2.20 caption (page=49, '... at 1 atm'), already held as R301. B1, B2, B5, B7, B12 are never named with a pressure. Page=30, Figure 2.7 text: 'flame spread over 100-µm-thick PMMA sheet for the ambient conditions of 20.7 percent O2, 1 atm, and an opposed-flow velocity of 2.5 cm/s' names no test; the 2/19/2014 100-µm samples are B1 and B3 (Air display 5 and 2, neither 2.5) and further 100-µm samples were run on later days (B6, B9, B15, B16, B19, B20), so it cannot be tied. Pages 21 and 31 ('In the first test ... a second test was done under the same conditions') state no pressure. Page=46 '99.2 to 99.5 kPa in the tests reported' (held as R302) and page=102 '1 atm' (SIBAL, held as R303) do not name B tests. Table A.1 (pages 111-112) has no pressure column.

Table A.1 observation cells (pages 111-112) state no flow in cm/s for these rows, or only the ignition flow: B21 'Ignition at 5 cm/s then fan pot turned down slowly', B22 'Ignition at 5 cm/s then decreased flow in step, fan pot 1.7, 0.5, 0.4, 0.36 (flame out)' (lower end in pot only). B10, B11, B13: 'Multiple velocities for steady spread, extinguished at pot 0.35'. Chapter 2 extinction-velocity sentences (pages 21-23, 31-33: about 1 cm/s for 100, 200, 300 µm, about 1.5 cm/s for 400 µm; about 2.6 and 4 cm/s at 16 percent O2) give limits by thickness, not per test id. Page=48 '100-µm-thick samples ... the opposing flow velocity is 3 cm/s' names no test. Air display cells not used (insufficient, per task).
